1.a) 
Describe the structure of ecosystem.
 
Ans: Structure of ecosystem: 
The structure of an ecosystem can be split into two main components, namely:  
Biotic Components and Abiotic Components. 
Biotic structure includes plants, animals & microorganisms present in an ecosystem.  
These organisms have different nutritional behavior and status in the ecosystem and are 
known as Autotrophs (Producers), Heterotrophs (Consumers) & Micro-consumers 
(Decomposers) based on how they get their food.  
Abiotic components are the non-living component of an ecosystem.  It includes air, water, 
soil, minerals, sunlight, temperature, nutrients, wind, altitude, turbidity, etc.

3.a) 
How N2 cycle maintain proper functioning of the ecosystem? 
Ans. Nitrogen cycle 
Nitrogen cycle is that biogeochemical cycle through which the movement of nitrogen occurs 
between biotic (living) and abiotic (lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere) components of 
the ecosystem.  
Process of Nitrogen Cycle consists of the following steps .. 
1. Nitrogen fixation:  Nitrogen from the atmosphere is converted into ammonia and 
other nitrogeneous compound by certain bacterial species like Rhizobium, 
Azotobacter, etc. and by other natural phenomena. 
1. Assimilation:  Nitrogen in the form of nitrite ions, nitrate ions or ammonium ions 
enters in the plant and animal body. 
2. Ammonification: After the death of plants and animals nitrogen present in organic 
matter converts to ammonium compounds by ammonifying bacteria, 
3. Nitrification: Nitrites and nitrate salts are formed by the oxidation of ammonia with 
the help of Nitrosomonas bacteria species. 
4. Denitrification: Inorganic N2 is produced  from nitrate /nitrite salts by denitrifying 
bacteriaand released into the atmosphere

5.a) 
Define biodiversity. Give various levels of biodiversity. 
Ans. Biodiversity is the variety and variability of life on Earth. It means “the existence of a
large number of different kinds of animals and plants which make a balanced 
environment” 
Biodiversity is usually considered at three different levels……. 
1. Genetic diversity 
The variety of genes within a given species  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2. Species diversity 
The variety of species in a given ecosystem.  
Diversity is greatest when all the species present are equally abundant in the area. 
A large number of plants, animals and microorganisms interact with each other in a 
ecosystem.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
3 
3

3. Ecosystem diversity 
The variety of ecosystem in a given region 
Ecosystem diversity deals with the variations in ecosystems within a geographical 
location and its overall impact on human existence and the environment. 
An example of ecological diversity on a global scale would be the variation in ecosystems, 
such as deserts, forests, grasslands, wetlands and oceans.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
b) 
Why food web is more important ecologically than the concept of simple 
food chain.
2 
2 
1 
Ans. The transfer of food energy from the producers ( plants ) through a series of organisms 
(Herbivores, Carnivores) successively with the repeated activities of eating and being eaten 
is known as food chain.  
Whereas food web is a network of food chains where different types of organisms are 
connected at different trophic levels so that there are a number of options of eating and being 
eaten at each trophic level.  
So, food webs improve the stability of an ecosystem as it includes all the interconnected 
food chains. These webs are important for illustrating the feeding relationships in a 
community among the species. 
A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which food and its contained energy 
pass. If one of the organisms number decreases in a linear food chain, next organisms will be 
affected due to food shortage.  
However, in a food web, each organism has a choice to feed on different types of other 
organisms. So,   the concept of the food web is more significant that food chain.

(iv) Ethical value 
Ethical and moral value is based on the importance of protecting all forms of life. 
It involves ethical issues like ‘’All life must be preserved’’ 
The ethical value means that a species may or may not be used, but its existence in 
our nature gives us pleasure. 
Ex: 1. The river Ganga is considered as holy river. 
2. Vembu, Tulsi are some of the trees worshipped by the Tamilans. 
3. We are not deriving anything from Kangaroo, Zebra, but we feel that these should 
exist in nature. 
(v) Aesthetic value 
The beautiful nature of plants & animals insist us to protect the biodiversity.  
Ex: People from far and wide spend a lot of time and money to visit beautiful areas 
where they can enjoy the aesthetic value of biodiversity and this type of tourism is 
now known as ecotourism.  
The pleasant music of world birds, colour of flowers, peacock, and butterfly are 
important aesthetic value. 
(vi) Option value 
It includes the potential of biodiversity that are presently unknown and need to be 
explored. The optional values of biodiversity suggest that any species may be proved 
to be a valuable after someday. ( i.e., presently unknown but need to be known)  
Eg., growing Biotechnology field is searching a species which can cure diseases like 
cancer and AIDS. 
b) 
What are alternative energy resources? How it fulfill the future energy 
need. 
Ans. The energy resources that can be regenerated easily through natural process once 
they are used up are called the renewable or alternative energy resources.  
Renewable energy resources include solar energy, wind power, hydropower etc. 
As the conventional fossil fuel energies like coal, petroleum, natural gas and nuclear 
energy are not abundant and one day will be exhausted, so we should depend more on 
the alternative non-conventional energy resources. The advantages of alternative 
energies are 
(i) They are plenty in sources 
(ii) Non-polluting and eco-friendly 
These types of energy can fulfill our future energy demand. 
Various types of alternative energy resources are 
• 
Solar energy
